en.h1: Period Mode: stay close to your worship during your period
summary: Period Mode is the part of Lunora that follows your cycle alongside your prayer, Quran and dhikr: it tracks your period and estimates the next one, turns off the adhan sound, rests Protect My Prayer and counts the Ramadan fasts you will make up. It also shows what the Hanafi, Shafi’i, Maliki and Hanbali schools say about reading the Quran during menstruation, with their sources, and puts your own school first if you choose one. Lunora is an Islamic app for Muslim women on iPhone and Android.

shot.alt: Lunora's Period Mode: the My Cycle screen showing day 3 of 7 inside a floral ring

what.h2: Your cycle and your worship, in one place
what.p: No guilt and no guesswork: the app keeps track, explains what changes and what doesn’t, and leaves rulings to scholars.

cards.p: Mark your days on a cycle ring, see an estimate of your next period based on your own average, and get a gentle “Has your period ended?” on the estimated last day.
The Period guide sets out the Hanafi, Shafi’i, Maliki and Hanbali views on reading and touching the Quran, naming its sources.
Period Mode asks about days that fell in Ramadan. The Qada screen counts recorded, kept and remaining fasts and can remind you the evening before the day you pick.
Dua and dhikr suggestions that fit your mood, hadith and fiqh cards, verses for comfort, and one of the 99 Names each day.
Ghusl step by step, and a single reminder when you mark your period as over, for whenever you’re ready.
The adhan sound is off, Protect My Prayer rests, your prayer streak is kept, and you can pause your Quran reading plan.
Set your situation to pregnant, postpartum, breastfeeding or irregular, and the estimate adapts or steps aside. Postpartum mode counts the days until you mark that your bleeding has stopped.
Log how you feel each day. With Lunora+ you also get cycle insights and a document of your records to share with your doctor.
Your period, mood and symptom records stay on your device in its secure storage and are never uploaded. No account is needed.

how.h2: From the first day to ghusl

steps.p: When your period begins, mark it in Period Mode. The adhan sound goes quiet and Protect My Prayer rests from that moment.

steps.h3: Tell Lunora what applies to you
steps.p: Optionally choose your situation and your madhhab. You can leave either unstated and change them any time.
Log symptoms, mood and notes, and get duas and dhikr that fit how you feel. The guide explains what is lifted during menstruation and what is not.
On the estimated last day Lunora asks whether your period has ended. Once you mark it, you can get one ghusl reminder for when you’re ready.
If your period fell in Ramadan, Period Mode asks about those days and adds them to your qada fasts.

details.h2: What Lunora shows for each madhhab
details.p: Lunora does not issue rulings. It shows what each school is reported to hold, names where that comes from, and suggests asking a scholar about your own situation.

ps: The Period guide lists the view of each of the four schools on touching the mushaf, reciting, reading verses with the intention of dua or dhikr, and listening.

items.h3: Your madhhab, only if you say so
ps: If you choose your madhhab in Period Mode settings, its view is shown first. You can also choose “I would rather not say”.
Lunora never guesses your madhhab from your country. Without one, the app shows no school-specific numbers.
If you have chosen a madhhab and your bleeding goes on for a while, a card shows the maximum length of menstruation that school is commonly reported to recognize.
The card says plainly: “This is not a ruling. For your situation, please consult a knowledgeable scholar.”
The “What is lifted, and what is not” section explains that the prayers of menstruation days are not made up, while missed fasts are.
The qada counter only counts days: “When and how to make them up depends on your school of thought (madhhab); ask a scholar about that.”

items.q: What is Period Mode in Lunora?
items.a: Period Mode is the part of the Lunora app that follows your menstrual cycle alongside your prayer, Quran and dhikr. It tracks your cycle and estimates the next period, explains what changes in worship during menstruation, offers duas and dhikr that fit your mood, and counts qada fasts. Lunora is available on iPhone and Android.

items.q: Does Lunora follow the four madhhabs?
items.a: Lunora shows the views of the Hanafi, Shafi'i, Maliki and Hanbali schools rather than a single answer. Its Period guide lists each school's view on reading the Quran during menstruation together with the source, and shows your school first if you have chosen one. The app does not issue rulings and suggests asking a scholar about your own situation.

items.q: Can Lunora track the fasts I need to make up after my period?
items.a: Yes. Period Mode asks about period days that fell in Ramadan, and the Qada screen shows how many fasts are recorded, kept and remaining. You can pick a day for your next qada fast and get a reminder the evening before. Lunora only counts the days; when and how to make them up depends on your madhhab.

items.q: What happens to the adhan and Protect My Prayer during my period?
items.a: While Period Mode is on, the adhan sound is turned off and Protect My Prayer rests without asking. Both return on their own when your period ends, and period days do not break your prayer streak.

items.q: Is my period data private?
items.a: Yes. Your period, mood, symptom and journal records stay on your device in its secure storage and are not uploaded to Lunora's servers. No account is needed and there are no ads.

items.q: Does Period Mode work during pregnancy or after giving birth?
items.a: Yes. You can set your situation to pregnant, postpartum, breastfeeding or irregular. The estimate adapts or pauses accordingly, and postpartum mode counts the days until you mark that your bleeding has stopped.

cards.p: Count dhikr from your home screen, with a sourced dhikr library and the 99 Names.
Khatam plans for Ramadan, 60 days or a year, and plans you build yourself.
At prayer time the apps you choose wait until you mark your prayer.

shot.alt: Lunora Dönem Modu: çiçekli halkanın içinde 7 günün 3. günü gösteren Döngüm ekranı

what.p: Suçluluk yok, tahmin yürütmek yok: uygulama takibi yapar, neyin değişip neyin değişmediğini anlatır, hükmü âlimlere bırakır.

cards.p: Günlerinizi döngü halkasında işaretleyin, kendi ortalamanıza göre bir sonraki dönemin tahminini görün; tahmini son günde nazik bir “Âdetin bitti mi?” sorusu gelir.
Dönem rehberi, Hanefî, Şâfiî, Mâlikî ve Hanbelî mezheplerinin Kur'an okuma ve mushafa dokunmaya dair görüşlerini kaynaklarıyla verir.
Dönem Modu, Ramazan'a denk gelen günleri size sorar. Kaza ekranı kaydedilen, tutulan ve kalan oruçları sayar; seçtiğiniz günden bir akşam önce hatırlatabilir.
Ruh hâlinize uygun dua ve zikir önerileri, hadis ve fıkıh kartları, teselli veren ayetler ve her gün Esmâ-i Hüsnâ'dan bir isim.
Adım adım gusül ve âdetinizin bittiğini işaretlediğinizde, hazır olduğunuz an için tek bir hatırlatma.
Ezan sesi kapanır, Namazımı Koru dinlenir, namaz seriniz korunur ve Kur'an okuma planınızı duraklatabilirsiniz.
Durumunuzu hamile, lohusa, emziren ya da düzensiz olarak seçin; tahmin buna göre uyum sağlar ya da kenara çekilir. Lohusalık modu, kanamanın kesildiğini işaretleyene kadar günleri sayar.
Her gün nasıl hissettiğinizi kaydedin. Lunora+ ile döngü analizi ve doktorunuzla paylaşabileceğiniz bir kayıt belgesi de gelir.
Dönem, ruh hâli ve belirti kayıtlarınız cihazınızın güvenli depolamasında kalır, hiçbir yere yüklenmez. Hesap gerekmez.

steps.p: Âdetiniz başlayınca Dönem Modu'nda işaretleyin. O andan itibaren ezan sesi susar, Namazımı Koru dinlenir.
İsterseniz durumunuzu ve mezhebinizi seçin. İkisini de belirtmeden bırakabilir, istediğiniz zaman değiştirebilirsiniz.
Belirti, ruh hâli ve not kaydedin; nasıl hissettiğinize uygun dua ve zikirler alın. Rehber, âdet hâlinde neyin kalkıp neyin kalmadığını anlatır.
Tahmini son günde Lunora âdetinizin bitip bitmediğini sorar. İşaretlediğinizde, hazır olduğunuzda gusül için tek bir hatırlatma alabilirsiniz.
Âdetiniz Ramazan'a denk geldiyse Dönem Modu o günleri sorar ve kaza oruçlarınıza ekler.

details.h2: Lunora her mezhep için ne gösterir
details.p: Lunora hüküm vermez. Her mezhebin görüşü olarak aktarılanı, nereden geldiğini belirterek gösterir ve kendi durumunuz için bir ilim ehline danışmanızı önerir.

ps: Dönem rehberi dört mezhebin her biri için mushafa dokunma, Kur'an'ı tilavet etme, ayetleri dua ya da zikir niyetiyle okuma ve dinleme konusundaki görüşü listeler.
Dönem Modu ayarlarındaki “Mezhebim” satırından mezhebinizi seçerseniz onun görüşü en üstte gösterilir. “Belirtmek istemiyorum” da diyebilirsiniz.
Lunora mezhebinizi asla ülkenizden tahmin etmez. Mezhep seçilmemişse uygulama mezhebe özgü hiçbir sayı göstermez.
Mezhebinizi seçtiyseniz ve kanamanız bir süredir devam ediyorsa, bir kart o mezhepte hayız için anılan azami süreyi gösterir.
Kartta açıkça şu yazar: “Bu bir hüküm değildir. Durumun için bir ilim ehline danışmanı öneririz.”
“Ne kalkar, ne kalmaz” bölümü, hayız günlerinin namazının kaza edilmediğini, orucun ise kaza edildiğini anlatır.
Kaza sayacı yalnız günleri sayar: “Lunora yalnız günleri sayar. Kazanın ne zaman ve nasıl tutulacağı mezheplere göre değişir; bunun için bir hocaya danış.”

items.a: Dönem Modu, Lunora uygulamasının âdet döngünüzü namaz, Kur'an ve zikirle birlikte takip eden bölümüdür. Döngünüzü kaydeder ve bir sonraki dönemi tahmin eder, âdet hâlinde ibadette neyin değiştiğini anlatır, ruh hâlinize uygun dua ve zikirler önerir ve kaza oruçlarını sayar. items.a: Lunora tek bir cevap yerine Hanefî, Şâfiî, Mâlikî ve Hanbelî mezheplerinin görüşlerini gösterir. Dönem rehberi, her mezhebin âdet hâlinde Kur'an okumaya dair görüşünü kaynağıyla birlikte listeler ve mezhebinizi seçtiyseniz onu en üstte gösterir. Uygulama hüküm vermez; kendi durumunuz için bir ilim ehline danışmanızı önerir.

items.q: Lunora âdet yüzünden tutamadığım oruçları takip edebilir mi?
items.a: Evet. Dönem Modu Ramazan'a denk gelen âdet günlerinizi sorar; Kaza ekranı kaydedilen, tutulan ve kalan oruç sayısını gösterir. Bir sonraki kaza orucunuz için gün seçip bir akşam önce hatırlatma alabilirsiniz. Lunora yalnız günleri sayar; kazanın ne zaman ve nasıl tutulacağı mezhebinize göre değişir.

items.q: Âdet günlerimde ezana ve Namazımı Koru'ya ne olur?
items.a: Dönem Modu açıkken ezan sesi kapanır ve Namazımı Koru size sormadan dinlenir. Dönem bitince ikisi de kendiliğinden geri gelir; dönem günleri namaz serinizi de bozmaz.

items.a: Evet. Dönem, ruh hâli, belirti ve günlük kayıtlarınız cihazınızın güvenli depolamasında kalır ve Lunora'nın sunucularına yüklenmez. Hesap gerekmez, reklam yoktur.

items.q: Dönem Modu hamilelikte ya da doğumdan sonra çalışıyor mu?
items.a: Evet. Durumunuzu hamile, lohusa, emziren ya da düzensiz olarak belirleyebilirsiniz. Tahmin buna göre uyum sağlar ya da bekler; lohusalık modu ise kanamanın kesildiğini işaretleyene kadar günleri sayar.

de.h1: Periodenmodus: Bleib deiner Ibada auch während deiner Periode nah
summary: Der Periodenmodus ist der Teil von Lunora, der deinen Zyklus neben deinem Gebet, Koran und Dhikr begleitet: Er hält deine Periode fest und schätzt die nächste, schaltet den Adhan-Ton aus, lässt „Mein Gebet schützen“ ruhen und zählt die Ramadan-Fastentage, die du nachholen wirst. Außerdem zeigt er, was die hanafitische, schafiitische, malikitische und hanbalitische Rechtsschule zum Koranlesen während der Menstruation sagen, mit ihren Quellen, und stellt deine eigene Rechtsschule an den Anfang, wenn du eine wählst. Lunora ist eine islamische App für muslimische Frauen, kostenlos für iPhone und Android.

shot.alt: Der Periodenmodus von Lunora: der Bildschirm „Mein Zyklus“ zeigt Tag 3 von 7 in einem Blumenring

what.h2: Dein Zyklus und deine Ibada an einem Ort
what.p: Keine Schuldgefühle und kein Rätselraten: Die App behält den Überblick, erklärt, was sich ändert und was nicht, und überlässt Rechtsurteile den Gelehrten.

cards.p: Markiere deine Tage auf einem Zyklusring, sieh eine Schätzung deiner nächsten Periode auf Grundlage deines eigenen Durchschnitts und erhalte am geschätzten letzten Tag ein sanftes „Ist deine Periode vorbei?“.
Der Periodenratgeber legt die hanafitische, schafiitische, malikitische und hanbalitische Ansicht zum Lesen und Berühren des Korans dar und nennt seine Quellen.

Der Periodenmodus fragt nach Tagen, die in den Ramadan fielen. Der Bildschirm „Nachholen“ (Qada) zählt erfasste, nachgeholte und verbleibende Fastentage und kann dich am Abend vor dem Tag erinnern, den du wählst.
Dua- und Dhikr-Vorschläge passend zu deiner Stimmung, Hadith- und Fiqh-Karten, tröstende Verse und jeden Tag einer der 99 Namen.
Ghusl Schritt für Schritt und eine einzige Erinnerung, wenn du deine Periode als beendet markierst, für den Moment, in dem du bereit bist.
Der Adhan-Ton ist aus, „Mein Gebet schützen“ ruht, deine Gebetsserie bleibt erhalten, und du kannst deinen Koran-Leseplan pausieren.

Stell deine Situation auf schwanger, Wochenbett, stillend oder unregelmäßig, und die Schätzung passt sich an oder tritt zurück. Der Wochenbett-Modus zählt die Tage, bis du markierst, dass deine Blutung aufgehört hat.
Halte jeden Tag fest, wie du dich fühlst. Mit Lunora+ bekommst du außerdem Zyklus-Auswertungen und ein Dokument deiner Einträge, das du mit deiner Ärztin oder deinem Arzt teilen kannst.
Deine Perioden-, Stimmungs- und Symptomeinträge bleiben im sicheren Speicher deines Geräts und werden nie hochgeladen. Du brauchst kein Konto.

how.h2: Vom ersten Tag bis zum Ghusl

steps.p: Wenn deine Periode beginnt, markiere sie im Periodenmodus. Ab diesem Moment ist der Adhan-Ton still und „Mein Gebet schützen“ ruht.

steps.h3: Sag Lunora, was für dich gilt
steps.p: Wähle auf Wunsch deine Situation und deine Rechtsschule. Du kannst beides offenlassen und jederzeit ändern.
Halte Symptome, Stimmung und Notizen fest und erhalte Duas und Dhikr, die zu deinem Befinden passen. Der Ratgeber erklärt, was während der Menstruation entfällt und was nicht.
Am geschätzten letzten Tag fragt Lunora, ob deine Periode vorbei ist. Sobald du es markierst, kannst du eine Ghusl-Erinnerung für den Moment bekommen, in dem du bereit bist.
Wenn deine Periode in den Ramadan fiel, fragt der Periodenmodus nach diesen Tagen und fügt sie deinen Qada-Fastentagen hinzu.

details.h2: Was Lunora für jede Rechtsschule zeigt
details.p: Lunora spricht keine Rechtsurteile. Die App zeigt, welche Ansicht jeder Rechtsschule zugeschrieben wird, nennt, woher das stammt, und empfiehlt, für deine eigene Situation Gelehrte zu fragen.

ps: Der Periodenratgeber führt für jede der vier Rechtsschulen die Ansicht zum Berühren des Mushafs, zum Rezitieren, zum Lesen von Versen mit der Absicht von Dua oder Dhikr und zum Zuhören auf.

items.h3: Deine Rechtsschule, nur wenn du es sagst
ps: Wenn du in den Einstellungen des Periodenmodus deine Rechtsschule wählst, wird ihre Ansicht zuerst gezeigt. Du kannst auch „Ich möchte es nicht angeben“ wählen.
Lunora leitet deine Rechtsschule nie aus deinem Land ab. Ohne gewählte Rechtsschule zeigt die App keine schulspezifischen Zahlen.
Wenn du eine Rechtsschule gewählt hast und deine Blutung eine Weile anhält, zeigt eine Karte die Höchstdauer der Menstruation, die diese Rechtsschule nach verbreiteter Angabe anerkennt.
Die Karte sagt klar: „Dies ist kein Rechtsspruch. Wende dich für deine Lage an sachkundige Gelehrte.“
Der Abschnitt „Was entfällt, und was nicht“ erklärt, dass die Gebete der Menstruationstage nicht nachgeholt werden, versäumte Fastentage dagegen schon.
Der Qada-Zähler zählt nur die Tage: „Wann und wie man sie nachholt, unterscheidet sich je nach Rechtsschule; frag dazu eine kundige Person.“

items.q: Was ist der Periodenmodus in Lunora?
items.a: Der Periodenmodus ist der Teil der App Lunora, der deinen Menstruationszyklus neben deinem Gebet, Koran und Dhikr begleitet. Er verfolgt deinen Zyklus und schätzt die nächste Periode, erklärt, was sich während der Menstruation bei der Ibada ändert, bietet Duas und Dhikr passend zu deiner Stimmung an und zählt Qada-Fastentage. Lunora kannst du kostenlos für iPhone und Android herunterladen.

items.q: Folgt Lunora den vier Rechtsschulen?
items.a: Lunora zeigt die Ansichten der hanafitischen, schafiitischen, malikitischen und hanbalitischen Rechtsschule statt einer einzigen Antwort. Der Periodenratgeber führt die Ansicht jeder Rechtsschule zum Koranlesen während der Menstruation samt Quelle auf und zeigt deine Rechtsschule zuerst, wenn du eine gewählt hast. Die App spricht keine Rechtsurteile und empfiehlt, für deine eigene Situation Gelehrte zu fragen.

items.q: Kann Lunora die Fastentage festhalten, die ich nach meiner Periode nachholen muss?
items.a: Ja. Der Periodenmodus fragt nach Periodentagen, die in den Ramadan fielen, und der Bildschirm „Nachholen“ (Qada) zeigt, wie viele Fastentage erfasst, nachgeholt und noch offen sind. Du kannst einen Tag für dein nächstes Qada-Fasten wählen und am Abend davor eine Erinnerung bekommen. Lunora zählt nur die Tage; wann und wie du sie nachholst, hängt von deiner Rechtsschule ab.

items.q: Was passiert während meiner Periode mit dem Adhan und mit „Mein Gebet schützen“?
items.a: Solange der Periodenmodus an ist, ist der Adhan-Ton ausgeschaltet und „Mein Gebet schützen“ ruht, ohne zu fragen. Beides kehrt von selbst zurück, wenn deine Periode endet, und Periodentage unterbrechen deine Gebetsserie nicht.

items.q: Bleiben meine Periodendaten privat?
items.a: Ja. Deine Perioden-, Stimmungs-, Symptom- und Tagebucheinträge bleiben im sicheren Speicher deines Geräts und werden nicht auf die Server von Lunora hochgeladen. Du brauchst kein Konto, und es gibt keine Werbung.

items.q: Funktioniert der Periodenmodus in der Schwangerschaft oder nach der Geburt?
items.a: Ja. Du kannst deine Situation auf schwanger, Wochenbett, stillend oder unregelmäßig stellen. Die Schätzung passt sich entsprechend an oder pausiert, und der Wochenbett-Modus zählt die Tage, bis du markierst, dass deine Blutung aufgehört hat.

fr.h1: Mode règles : reste proche de ton adoration pendant tes règles
summary: Le Mode règles est la partie de Lunora qui suit ton cycle aux côtés de ta prière, du Coran et du dhikr : il enregistre tes règles et estime les prochaines, coupe le son de l’adhan, met Protéger ma prière en pause et compte les jeûnes du Ramadan que tu devras rattraper. Il montre aussi ce que disent les écoles hanafite, chaféite, malékite et hanbalite sur la lecture du Coran pendant les menstrues, avec leurs sources, et place ta propre école en premier si tu en choisis une. Lunora est une application islamique pensée pour les femmes musulmanes, gratuite à télécharger sur iPhone et Android.

shot.alt: Le Mode règles de Lunora : l’écran Mon cycle affichant le jour 3 sur 7 dans un anneau fleuri

what.h2: Ton cycle et ton adoration, au même endroit
what.p: Pas de culpabilité, pas de suppositions : l’app tient le compte, explique ce qui change et ce qui ne change pas, et laisse les avis juridiques aux savants.

cards.p: Marque tes jours sur un anneau de cycle, vois une estimation de tes prochaines règles basée sur ta propre moyenne, et reçois un doux « Tes règles sont-elles terminées ? » le dernier jour estimé.
Le Guide des règles présente les avis hanafite, chaféite, malékite et hanbalite sur la lecture et le toucher du Coran, en citant ses sources.

Le Mode règles te demande quels jours sont tombés pendant le Ramadan. L’écran Rattrapage compte les jeûnes enregistrés, accomplis et restants, et peut te le rappeler la veille au soir du jour que tu choisis.
Des suggestions d’invocations et de dhikr adaptées à ton humeur, des cartes de hadith et de fiqh, des versets de réconfort, et l’un des 99 Noms chaque jour.
Le ghusl étape par étape, et un seul rappel quand tu indiques la fin de tes règles, pour le moment où tu seras prête.
Le son de l’adhan est coupé, Protéger ma prière se met en pause, ta série de prières est préservée, et tu peux mettre en pause ton plan de lecture du Coran.

cards.h3: À chaque étape de la vie
cards.p: Indique ta situation : enceinte, post-partum, allaitement ou cycle irrégulier, et l’estimation s’adapte ou s’efface. Le mode post-partum compte les jours jusqu’à ce que tu indiques que tes saignements se sont arrêtés.
Note chaque jour comment tu te sens. Avec Lunora+, tu as aussi des analyses de ton cycle et un document de tes données à partager avec ton médecin.
Tes données de règles, d’humeur et de symptômes restent sur ton appareil, dans son stockage sécurisé, et ne sont jamais envoyées en ligne. Aucun compte n’est nécessaire.

steps.p: Quand tes règles commencent, indique-le dans le Mode règles. Dès ce moment, le son de l’adhan se tait et Protéger ma prière se met en pause.

steps.h3: Dis à Lunora ce qui s’applique à toi
steps.p: Si tu veux, choisis ta situation et ton madhhab. Tu peux ne rien préciser pour l’un comme pour l’autre, et les changer à tout moment.
Note tes symptômes, ton humeur et tes notes, et reçois des invocations et du dhikr adaptés à ce que tu ressens. Le guide explique ce qui est levé pendant les menstrues et ce qui ne l’est pas.
Le dernier jour estimé, Lunora te demande si tes règles sont terminées. Une fois que tu l’as indiqué, tu peux recevoir un rappel unique pour le ghusl, quand tu seras prête.
Si tes règles sont tombées pendant le Ramadan, le Mode règles te demande quels jours et les ajoute à tes jeûnes à rattraper.

details.h2: Ce que Lunora montre pour chaque madhhab
details.p: Lunora ne rend pas d’avis juridiques. Elle montre ce que chaque école est rapportée tenir, indique d’où cela vient, et te suggère de consulter un savant pour ta propre situation.

items.h3: Lire le Coran pendant les menstrues
ps: Le Guide des règles présente l’avis de chacune des quatre écoles sur le fait de toucher le mushaf, de réciter, de lire des versets avec l’intention de l’invocation ou du dhikr, et d’écouter.

items.h3: Ton madhhab, seulement si tu le dis
ps: Si tu choisis ton madhhab dans les réglages du Mode règles, son avis s’affiche en premier. Tu peux aussi choisir « Je préfère ne pas le dire ».
Lunora ne devine jamais ton madhhab d’après ton pays. Sans madhhab choisi, l’app n’affiche aucun chiffre propre à une école.

items.h3: Quand les saignements durent plus longtemps
ps: Si tu as choisi un madhhab et que tes saignements se prolongent, une carte indique la durée maximale des menstrues que cette école reconnaît selon ce qui est couramment rapporté.
La carte le dit clairement : « Ce n’est pas un avis juridique. Pour ta situation, consulte un savant. »
La section « Ce qui est levé, et ce qui ne l’est pas » explique que les prières des jours de menstrues ne se rattrapent pas, alors que les jeûnes manqués se rattrapent.
Le compteur de qada ne fait que compter les jours : « Quand et comment les rattraper varie selon les écoles ; demande à une enseignante. »

items.q: Qu’est-ce que le Mode règles dans Lunora ?
items.a: Le Mode règles est la partie de l’application Lunora qui suit ton cycle menstruel aux côtés de ta prière, du Coran et du dhikr. Il suit ton cycle et estime tes prochaines règles, explique ce qui change dans l’adoration pendant les menstrues, propose des invocations et du dhikr adaptés à ton humeur, et compte les jeûnes à rattraper. Lunora est gratuite à télécharger sur iPhone et Android.

items.q: Lunora suit-elle les quatre madhhabs ?
items.a: Lunora montre les avis des écoles hanafite, chaféite, malékite et hanbalite plutôt qu’une réponse unique. Son Guide des règles présente l’avis de chaque école sur la lecture du Coran pendant les menstrues, avec la source, et affiche ton école en premier si tu en as choisi une. L’app ne rend pas d’avis juridiques et te suggère de consulter un savant pour ta propre situation.

items.q: Lunora peut-elle suivre les jeûnes que je dois rattraper après mes règles ?
items.a: Oui. Le Mode règles te demande quels jours de règles sont tombés pendant le Ramadan, et l’écran Rattrapage indique combien de jeûnes sont enregistrés, accomplis et restants. Tu peux choisir un jour pour ton prochain jeûne de rattrapage et recevoir un rappel la veille au soir. Lunora ne fait que compter les jours ; quand et comment les rattraper dépend de ton madhhab.

items.q: Que deviennent l’adhan et Protéger ma prière pendant mes règles ?
items.a: Tant que le Mode règles est activé, le son de l’adhan est coupé et Protéger ma prière se met en pause sans te demander. Les deux reviennent tout seuls à la fin de tes règles, et les jours de règles ne cassent pas ta série de prières.

items.q: Mes données de règles restent-elles privées ?
items.a: Oui. Tes données de règles, d’humeur, de symptômes et de journal restent sur ton appareil, dans son stockage sécurisé, et ne sont pas envoyées sur les serveurs de Lunora. Aucun compte n’est nécessaire et il n’y a pas de publicité.

items.q: Le Mode règles fonctionne-t-il pendant la grossesse ou après l’accouchement ?
items.a: Oui. Tu peux indiquer ta situation : enceinte, post-partum, allaitement ou cycle irrégulier. L’estimation s’adapte ou se met en pause en conséquence, et le mode post-partum compte les jours jusqu’à ce que tu indiques que tes saignements se sont arrêtés.

cards.p: Compte ton dhikr depuis l’écran d’accueil, avec une bibliothèque de dhikr sourcée et les 99 Noms.
Des plans de khatm pour le Ramadan, en 60 jours ou en un an, et des plans que tu crées toi-même.
À l’heure de la prière, les applications que tu choisis attendent que tu marques ta prière.

en.h1: Protect My Prayer: your apps wait while you pray
summary: Protect My Prayer is a feature in Lunora that makes the apps you choose wait when a prayer time comes in, for 15 minutes by default. Tap “I prayed” and they open right away; if you don’t, they open on their own when the time is up, and on your period days the feature rests by itself. Lunora is an Islamic app for Muslim women on iPhone and Android.

shot.alt: Lunora's Protect My Prayer screen at Asr: “It’s prayer time. This app can wait a little.” with 12 minutes left

what.h2: A short pause at prayer time, on your terms
what.p: Not a ban and not a punishment: a few minutes in which the apps that pull you away wait for you.

cards.p: Apps wait 15 minutes by default, counted from the start of the prayer time. On Android you can choose 10, 15 or 20 minutes; on iPhone, 15 or 20.
Mark your prayer and the apps open straight away. The prayer is also marked in today’s prayers on the Today screen.
Nothing waits until you choose it. The Phone app and Lunora are never made to wait.
Pick the prayers you want protected. All five prayers are available with Lunora+.
While Period Mode is on, protection pauses without asking and returns when your period ends. Your choices stay exactly as they were.
Count the days you have marked all five prayers. Marking a missed prayer later counts too, and period days never break the streak.

how.h2: Set it up once, then let prayer time do the rest

steps.p: Open Protect My Prayer in Lunora and pick the apps that should wait at prayer time.
On iPhone, Apple asks for Screen Time permission. On Android, Lunora needs Usage access and permission to display over other apps.
Select the prayers to protect and how long the apps should wait.
If you open a chosen app, a calm screen appears instead: “It’s prayer time. This app can wait a little.”, with the minutes left.
Your apps open at once and the prayer is marked. If you’re running late, “I’ll pray in a moment” lets them open on their own when the time is up.

details.h2: How it works on each phone

ps: Protect My Prayer uses Apple’s Screen Time permission and needs iOS 16 or later. Setup has two steps: Screen Time permission, then choosing apps from Apple’s own list, where apps are grouped by category.
Your passcode stays with Apple; Lunora never sees it.
Setup has three steps: choose your apps, turn on Usage access, and allow Lunora to display over other apps so the waiting screen can appear.
Usage access lets Lunora see which app was opened: only its name, never what is inside. Nothing leaves your device.

details.note: If you need an app urgently, “An emergency? Lift it now” opens everything until the next prayer. And if a permission is switched off in your phone’s settings, Lunora tells you that protection has stopped instead of failing silently. You don’t need to keep Lunora open; opening it now and then is enough to keep protection set up.

items.q: What is Protect My Prayer?
items.a: Protect My Prayer is a feature in the Lunora app. When a prayer time comes in, the apps you have chosen wait for a short time, 15 minutes by default. When you tap “I prayed” in Lunora they open right away, and the prayer is marked in your prayer log.

items.q: How long do the apps stay locked?
items.a: 15 minutes by default, counted from the start of the prayer time. On Android you can choose 10, 15 or 20 minutes, and on iPhone 15 or 20. If you tap “I prayed” they open immediately; if you don't, they open on their own when the time is up.

items.q: Can I open an app in an emergency?
items.a: Yes. Tap “An emergency? Lift it now” and the apps open straight away; they are protected again at the next prayer. The Phone app and Lunora are never made to wait.

items.q: Does Protect My Prayer work on iPhone?
items.a: Yes. On iPhone it uses Apple's Screen Time permission and needs iOS 16 or later. On Android it uses Usage access and the permission to display over other apps.

items.q: What happens during my period?
items.a: Protect My Prayer rests on its own while Period Mode is on and comes back when your period ends. It doesn't ask you, your chosen apps and prayers are kept, and period days don't break your prayer streak.

items.q: Is Protect My Prayer free?
items.a: Lunora has no ads. Protect My Prayer for all five prayers comes with Lunora+, a subscription you can start with a free trial.

tr.h1: Namazımı Koru: namaz vaktinde uygulamalarınız bekler
summary: Namazımı Koru, Lunora'da namaz vakti girince seçtiğiniz uygulamaları kısa bir süre, varsayılan olarak 15 dakika bekleten özelliktir. “Kıldım” dediğinizde uygulamalar hemen açılır, demezseniz süre dolunca kendiliğinden açılır; âdet günlerinizde ise koruma kendiliğinden dinlenir. shot.alt: Lunora Namazımı Koru ekranı, ikindi vakti: “Namaz vakti. Bu uygulama biraz beklesin.” 12 dakika kaldı

what.h2: Namaz vaktinde kısa bir mola, sizin kurallarınızla
what.p: Ne bir yasak ne bir ceza: sizi namazdan alıkoyan uygulamaların birkaç dakika sizi beklemesi.

cards.p: Uygulamalar varsayılan olarak vaktin girişinden itibaren 15 dakika bekler. Android'de 10, 15 ya da 20 dakika, iPhone'da 15 ya da 20 dakika seçebilirsiniz.
Namazınızı işaretleyin, uygulamalar hemen açılsın. Namaz, Bugün ekranındaki günün namazlarında da işaretlenir.
Siz seçmedikçe hiçbir şey beklemez. Telefon uygulaması ve Lunora hiçbir zaman beklemez.
Korunmasını istediğiniz vakitleri seçin. Beş vaktin tamamı Lunora+ ile açılır.
Dönem Modu açıkken koruma size sormadan durur, dönem bitince kendiliğinden döner. Seçimleriniz olduğu gibi kalır.
Beş vakti işaretlediğiniz günler sayılır. Geçmiş bir vakti sonradan işaretlemek de sayılır; dönem günleri seriyi bozmaz.

how.h2: Bir kez kurun, gerisini vakit halletsin

steps.p: Lunora'da Namazımı Koru'yu açın ve namaz vaktinde beklemesini istediğiniz uygulamaları seçin.
iPhone'da Apple, Ekran Süresi izni ister. Android'de Lunora'nın Kullanım erişimine ve diğer uygulamaların üzerinde gösterme iznine ihtiyacı vardır.
Korunacak vakitleri ve uygulamaların ne kadar bekleyeceğini belirleyin.
Seçtiğiniz bir uygulamayı açarsanız onun yerine sakin bir ekran çıkar: “Namaz vakti. Bu uygulama biraz beklesin.” Kalan dakikalar da görünür.
Uygulamalarınız hemen açılır ve namaz işaretlenir. Biraz gecikecekseniz “Birazdan kılacağım” dediğinizde uygulamalar süre dolunca kendiliğinden açılır.

ps: Namazımı Koru, Apple'ın Ekran Süresi iznini kullanır ve iOS 16 veya sonrasını gerektirir. Kurulum iki adımdır: Ekran Süresi izni, ardından uygulamaların kategorilere göre gruplandığı Apple'ın kendi listesinden seçim.
Telefon şifreniz Apple'da kalır; Lunora onu görmez.
Kurulum üç adımdır: uygulamaları seçin, Kullanım erişimini açın ve bekleme ekranının çıkabilmesi için Lunora'nın diğer uygulamaların üzerinde gösterilmesine izin verin.
Kullanım erişimi, Lunora'nın hangi uygulamanın açıldığını görmesini sağlar: yalnız uygulamanın adını görür, içine bakmaz. Hiçbir şey cihazınızdan çıkmaz.

details.note: Bir uygulamaya acilen ihtiyacınız olursa “Acil bir durum mu? Şimdi kaldır” ile bir sonraki vakte kadar her şey açılır. Telefon ayarlarından bir izin kapatılırsa Lunora korumanın durduğunu size söyler; sessizce çalışmayı bırakmaz. Lunora'yı açık tutmanız gerekmez, ara sıra açmanız korumanın kurulu kalması için yeterlidir.

items.q: Namazımı Koru nedir?
items.a: Namazımı Koru, Lunora uygulamasındaki bir özelliktir. Namaz vakti girince seçtiğiniz uygulamalar kısa bir süre, varsayılan olarak 15 dakika bekler. Lunora'da “Kıldım”a dokunduğunuzda hemen açılırlar ve namaz, namaz takibinizde işaretlenir.

items.q: Uygulamalar ne kadar süre kilitli kalır?
items.a: Varsayılan olarak vaktin girişinden itibaren 15 dakika. Android'de 10, 15 ya da 20 dakika, iPhone'da 15 ya da 20 dakika seçebilirsiniz. “Kıldım” derseniz hemen açılırlar; demezseniz süre dolunca kendiliğinden açılırlar.

items.q: Acil bir durumda uygulamayı açabilir miyim?
items.a: Evet. “Acil bir durum mu? Şimdi kaldır”a dokunduğunuzda uygulamalar hemen açılır ve bir sonraki vakitte yeniden korunur. Telefon uygulaması ve Lunora hiçbir zaman beklemez.

items.q: Namazımı Koru iPhone'da çalışıyor mu?
items.a: Evet. iPhone'da Apple'ın Ekran Süresi iznini kullanır ve iOS 16 veya sonrasını gerektirir. Android'de Kullanım erişimi ile diğer uygulamaların üzerinde gösterme iznini kullanır.

items.q: Âdet günlerimde ne olur?
items.a: Dönem Modu açıkken Namazımı Koru kendiliğinden dinlenir ve dönem bitince geri döner. Size sormaz; seçtiğiniz uygulamalar ve vakitler yerinde kalır, dönem günleri namaz serinizi de bozmaz.

items.a: Lunora, iPhone ve Android'de ücretsiz indirilir ve reklam içermez. Beş vaktin tamamında Namazımı Koru, ücretsiz denemeyle başlayabileceğiniz Lunora+ aboneliğiyle gelir.

de.h1: Mein Gebet schützen: Deine Apps warten, während du betest
summary: „Mein Gebet schützen“ ist eine Funktion in Lunora, die die Apps deiner Wahl warten lässt, wenn eine Gebetszeit beginnt, standardmäßig 15 Minuten. Tippe auf „Ich habe gebetet“, und sie öffnen sich sofort; tust du es nicht, öffnen sie sich von selbst, sobald die Zeit um ist, und an deinen Periodentagen ruht die Funktion von selbst. Lunora ist eine islamische App für muslimische Frauen, kostenlos für iPhone und Android.

shot.alt: Der Bildschirm „Mein Gebet schützen“ von Lunora zum Asr-Gebet: „Gebetszeit. Diese App kann kurz warten.“ mit noch 12 Minuten

what.h2: Eine kurze Pause zur Gebetszeit, nach deinen Regeln
what.p: Kein Verbot und keine Strafe: ein paar Minuten, in denen die Apps, die dich wegziehen, auf dich warten.

cards.p: Apps warten standardmäßig 15 Minuten, gerechnet ab Beginn der Gebetszeit. Auf Android kannst du 10, 15 oder 20 Minuten wählen, auf dem iPhone 15 oder 20.
Markiere dein Gebet, und die Apps öffnen sich sofort. Das Gebet wird auch bei den heutigen Gebeten auf dem Bildschirm „Heute“ markiert.
Nichts wartet, bevor du es auswählst. Die Telefon-App und Lunora müssen nie warten.
Wähle die Gebete, die geschützt werden sollen. Alle fünf Gebete gibt es mit Lunora+.
Solange der Periodenmodus an ist, pausiert der Schutz, ohne zu fragen, und kehrt zurück, wenn deine Periode endet. Deine Auswahl bleibt genau so, wie sie war.
Zähle die Tage, an denen du alle fünf Gebete markiert hast. Ein verpasstes Gebet später zu markieren zählt auch, und Periodentage unterbrechen die Serie nie.

how.h2: Einmal einrichten, den Rest übernimmt die Gebetszeit

steps.p: Öffne in Lunora „Mein Gebet schützen“ und wähle die Apps, die zur Gebetszeit warten sollen.
Auf dem iPhone fragt Apple nach der Bildschirmzeit-Berechtigung. Auf Android braucht Lunora den Nutzungszugriff und die Berechtigung, über anderen Apps angezeigt zu werden.
Wähle die Gebete, die geschützt werden sollen, und wie lange die Apps warten sollen.
Öffnest du eine gewählte App, erscheint stattdessen ein ruhiger Bildschirm: „Gebetszeit. Diese App kann kurz warten.“, mit den verbleibenden Minuten.

steps.h3: Bete, dann tippe auf „Ich habe gebetet“
steps.p: Deine Apps öffnen sich sofort, und das Gebet ist markiert. Wenn es bei dir später wird, sorgt „Ich bete gleich“ dafür, dass sie sich von selbst öffnen, sobald die Zeit um ist.

details.h2: So funktioniert es auf jedem Handy

ps: „Mein Gebet schützen“ nutzt Apples Bildschirmzeit-Berechtigung und braucht iOS 16 oder neuer. Die Einrichtung hat zwei Schritte: die Bildschirmzeit-Berechtigung, dann die Auswahl der Apps aus Apples eigener Liste, in der die Apps nach Kategorien gruppiert sind.
Dein Code bleibt bei Apple; Lunora sieht ihn nie.
Die Einrichtung hat drei Schritte: Apps wählen, den Nutzungszugriff einschalten und Lunora erlauben, über anderen Apps angezeigt zu werden, damit der Wartebildschirm erscheinen kann.
Mit dem Nutzungszugriff sieht Lunora, welche App geöffnet wurde: nur ihren Namen, nie ihren Inhalt. Nichts verlässt dein Gerät.

details.note: Wenn du eine App dringend brauchst, öffnet „Ein Notfall? Jetzt aufheben“ alles bis zum nächsten Gebet. Und wenn in den Einstellungen deines Handys eine Berechtigung ausgeschaltet wird, sagt dir Lunora, dass der Schutz gestoppt ist, statt still zu versagen. Du musst Lunora nicht geöffnet lassen; es reicht, die App ab und zu zu öffnen, damit der Schutz eingerichtet bleibt.

items.q: Was ist „Mein Gebet schützen“?
items.a: „Mein Gebet schützen“ ist eine Funktion der App Lunora. Wenn eine Gebetszeit beginnt, warten die Apps, die du gewählt hast, eine kurze Zeit, standardmäßig 15 Minuten. Wenn du in Lunora auf „Ich habe gebetet“ tippst, öffnen sie sich sofort, und das Gebet wird in deinem Gebetsprotokoll markiert.

items.q: Wie lange bleiben die Apps gesperrt?

cards.p: 30 days, one juz a day, each day starting from the first verse of its juz.
The whole Quran in two months: about ten pages of the Madinah mushaf a day, with the page numbers for each day.

how.h2: A plan that tells you what to read today

Read as a list with translation and transliteration, or as mushaf pages with the Madinah mushaf layout. When you finish, tap “I’ve read it”.

ps: All 114 surahs in Arabic with translation, as a list or as mushaf pages, with tajweed colours.

fr.h1: Plan de lecture du Coran et suivi du khatm
summary: Les plans de lecture de Lunora divisent le Coran en portions quotidiennes et suivent ta progression jour après jour, du khatm du Ramadan en 30 jours (un juz par jour) au khatm en 60 jours ou en un an. shot.alt: Aquarelle d’un Coran ouvert sur un rahle en bois, l’illustration que Lunora utilise pour son plan de khatm

what.h2: Dix plans prêts à l’emploi, ou le tien
what.p: Trois plans de khatm pour lire tout le Coran, sept plans plus courts, et un plan personnalisé construit avec les sourates que tu choisis.

cards.p: 30 jours, un juz par jour, chaque jour commençant au premier verset de son juz.
Tout le Coran en deux mois : environ dix pages du mushaf de Médine par jour, avec les numéros de page de chaque jour.
Une à deux pages par jour pendant 365 jours. Un peu chaque jour, sans t’arrêter.
Pour débuter (Al-Fatiha, puis de courtes sourates), Sourates du vendredi, Sourates du matin, Sourates de la nuit, Versets de guérison, Sourates apaisantes et 7 sourates en 7 jours.
Choisis les sourates, donne au plan un nom et une icône si tu veux, puis lis une ou deux sourates par jour ou fixe toi-même le nombre de jours.

cards.h3: À toi de choisir pendant tes règles
cards.p: Quand le Mode règles est activé, tu décides de mettre en pause ou de continuer. Un plan en pause ne fait pas avancer son compte de jours et reprend au même jour.

how.h2: Un plan qui te dit quoi lire aujourd’hui

steps.p: Ouvre Plans de lecture dans Lunora et commence un plan de khatm, un plan court, ou crée le tien.
Chaque jour indique exactement quoi lire : une plage de pages, un juz ou une sourate. Tout le plan est détaillé jour par jour.

steps.h3: Lis dans le lecteur de Coran
steps.p: Lis en liste avec la traduction et la translittération, ou en pages de mushaf avec la mise en page du mushaf de Médine. Quand tu as fini, touche « J’ai lu ».
Le plan montre à quel jour tu en es et le pourcentage accompli. Si tu passes à un autre plan, ta progression est conservée, et tu peux y revenir à tout moment.
Le dernier jour, Lunora marque le plan comme terminé, avec « Qu’Allah l’accepte ». Tu peux le recommencer ou choisir un autre plan.

ps: Les 114 sourates en arabe avec la traduction, en liste ou en pages de mushaf, avec les couleurs du tajwid.
Écoute cinq récitateurs, marque des versets, ajoute des notes et partage un verset sous forme de carte. D’autres récitateurs et l’écoute hors ligne par juz sont inclus dans Lunora+.
Le widget « Où tu t’es arrêtée » affiche la sourate et le verset où tu t’es arrêtée, pour reprendre ta lecture d’une seule touche.
Le plan Versets de guérison rassemble des versets lus avec l’intention de la guérison ; comme l’app le précise elle-même, ils ne remplacent pas un traitement.

items.q: Lunora permet-elle de suivre un khatm (hatim) ?
items.a: Oui. Lunora propose trois plans de khatm : le khatm du Ramadan (30 jours, un juz par jour), le khatm en 60 jours (environ dix pages par jour) et le khatm en un an (une à deux pages par jour). L’app indique à quel jour du plan tu en es et quelle part est accomplie.

items.q: Puis-je créer mon propre plan de lecture du Coran ?
items.a: Oui. Choisis les sourates que tu veux, ajoute un nom et une icône si tu le souhaites, puis lis une sourate par jour, deux par jour, ou fixe toi-même le nombre de jours. Un jour peut alors contenir plus d’une sourate.

items.q: Comment marquer un jour comme lu ?
items.a: Ouvre la lecture du jour depuis le plan, lis-la dans le lecteur de Coran de Lunora et touche « J’ai lu ». Le jour est marqué comme fait et le plan passe au suivant.

items.q: Que devient mon plan de lecture pendant mes règles ?
items.a: Si le Mode règles est activé, Lunora te laisse le choix : mettre le plan en pause ou continuer. Tant qu’il est en pause, le compte de jours n’avance pas, et il reprend au même jour quand tu désactives le Mode règles. Le plan renvoie aussi au guide du Mode règles, qui présente les avis des quatre madhhabs sur la lecture du Coran pendant les menstrues.

items.q: Quelle mise en page de mushaf Lunora utilise-t-elle ?
items.a: L’affichage en pages suit la mise en page du mushaf de Médine, en 604 pages, et les plans de khatm en 60 jours et en un an donnent leurs lectures quotidiennes sous forme de plages de pages de ce mushaf. La traduction et la translittération sont disponibles dans l’affichage en liste.

items.q: Lunora est-elle disponible sur iPhone et Android ?
items.a: Lunora est gratuite à télécharger sur l’App Store et Google Play, et sans publicité. Lunora+ est un abonnement qui ouvre l’application complète, et tu peux le commencer par un essai gratuit.

À l’heure de la prière, les applications que tu choisis attendent que tu marques ta prière.

what.h2: Your tasbih, on the home screen and in the app
what.p: Three dhikr widgets, a counter that keeps rounds and sets, and a library that tells you where each dhikr comes from.

cards.p: The “Tesbih with count” widget shows a ring of 33, the phrase you are saying and a + Count button. Tap the phrase to move to the next one, or ↺ to start the round again.

steps.h3: Start a dhikr in the app
steps.p: Open Dhikr in Lunora and choose a dhikr from the library, the tasbihat after prayer, morning or evening adhkar, or one you created.

From your phone’s widget gallery, add “Tesbih with count” or “Dhikr counter”.

The widget starts with the dhikr you last counted in the app, then offers six everyday phrases: SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, Allahu Akbar, La ilaha illallah, Astaghfirullah and salawat. Each tap shows on the widget straight away and is added to your daily count in Lunora.

ps: Counting from the widget works on iOS 17 and later, on the home screen and on the lock screen. On iOS 16 the widget still shows your count, and a tap opens the counter in the app.

items.q: Which dhikr can I count on the widget?

fr.h1: Widget dhikr et compteur de tasbih
summary: Lunora est une application islamique pensée pour les femmes musulmanes, avec un widget tasbih pour ton écran d’accueil : touche-le pour compter ton dhikr sans ouvrir l’application, et chaque touche s’ajoute au même total du jour que le compteur de l’app. Dans l’application, tu trouveras une bibliothèque de 113 dhikr avec le texte arabe, la translittération, le sens et la source, ainsi que tes propres séries de dhikr et les 99 Noms d’Allah. Lunora est gratuite à télécharger sur iPhone et Android.

shot.alt: Widgets Lunora sur l’écran d’accueil d’un iPhone, dont le widget tasbih qui affiche 21 sur 33

what.h2: Ton tasbih, sur l’écran d’accueil et dans l’app
what.p: Trois widgets de dhikr, un compteur qui gère les tours et les séries, et une bibliothèque qui te dit d’où vient chaque dhikr.

cards.p: Le widget « Tasbih avec compteur » affiche un anneau de 33, la formule que tu récites et un bouton + Compter. Touche la formule pour passer à la suivante, ou ↺ pour recommencer le tour.

cards.h3: Un anneau qui montre ta journée
cards.p: Le petit widget « Compteur de dhikr » montre combien de dhikr tu as fait aujourd’hui. Sur iPhone, il peut aussi se placer sur l’écran de verrouillage.
Un grand widget dessine ton dhikr sous forme de chapelet, avec les grains déjà comptés en couleur (Lunora+).

113 dhikr répartis en 16 catégories : après la prière, matin et soir, avant de dormir, voyage, maladie, détresse, istighfar, salawat, invocations Rabbana et plus encore. Chacun affiche le texte arabe, une translittération, le sens et sa source, par exemple « Muslim 591 ».
Écris ton propre dhikr ou choisis-en un dans la bibliothèque, fixe un objectif de 33, 99, 100, 1000 ou le nombre de ton choix, et crée des séries dont les étapes s’enchaînent.
Lis les Beaux Noms d’Allah avec leur sens, ou parcours les 99 dans l’ordre en les comptant, chaque touche faisant apparaître le nom suivant. Un widget « Le Nom du jour » est aussi disponible.

how.h2: De l’app à ton écran d’accueil

steps.p: Ouvre Dhikr dans Lunora et choisis un dhikr de la bibliothèque, les tasbihat après la prière, les adhkar du matin ou du soir, ou un dhikr que tu as créé.
Touche n’importe où sur le compteur. À l’objectif, le tour se termine et le compte repart à zéro ; dans une série, l’étape suivante commence. Beaucoup d’étapes ont aussi un audio que tu peux écouter.
Depuis la galerie de widgets de ton téléphone, ajoute « Tasbih avec compteur » ou « Compteur de dhikr ».

Le widget commence par le dernier dhikr que tu as compté dans l’app, puis propose six formules du quotidien : SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, Allahu Akbar, La ilaha illallah, Astaghfirullah et la salawat. Chaque touche s’affiche aussitôt sur le widget et s’ajoute à ton total du jour dans Lunora.

details.h2: Comment les widgets fonctionnent sur chaque téléphone

ps: Compter depuis le widget fonctionne à partir d’iOS 17, sur l’écran d’accueil et sur l’écran de verrouillage. Sous iOS 16, le widget affiche toujours ton total, et une touche ouvre le compteur dans l’app.
Touche le widget pour compter, comme sur iPhone. Le widget garde les touches et Lunora les intègre à ton total du jour, pour que rien ne soit compté deux fois.

items.q: Puis-je compter mon dhikr depuis l’écran d’accueil sans ouvrir l’application ?
items.a: Oui. Ajoute le widget « Tasbih avec compteur » de Lunora et touche + Compter ou l’anneau. Chaque touche est comptée sur le widget et ajoutée à ton total du jour dans l’app. Sur iPhone, il faut iOS 17 ou une version ultérieure ; sur les versions plus anciennes, une touche ouvre le compteur à la place.

items.q: Quels dhikr puis-je compter sur le widget ?
items.a: Le widget affiche d’abord le dernier dhikr que tu as compté dans l’app, puis six formules du quotidien : SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, Allahu Akbar, La ilaha illallah, Astaghfirullah et Allahumma salli ala Muhammad. Touche la formule pour passer à la suivante.

items.q: Lunora indique-t-elle d’où vient chaque dhikr ?
items.a: Oui. Chaque entrée de la bibliothèque de dhikr de Lunora indique sa source, par exemple un numéro de hadith chez Bukhari ou Muslim, avec le texte arabe, une translittération et le sens.

items.q: Lunora contient-elle les 99 Noms d’Allah (Asmaul Husna) ?
items.a: Oui. Tu peux lire les 99 Noms avec un sens court, les parcourir un par un dans l’ordre en les comptant, et ajouter un widget « Le Nom du jour ». L’app précise que le hadith sur les quatre-vingt-dix-neuf noms d’Allah est sahih, tandis que la liste des noms elle-même a été établie par les savants.

items.q: Puis-je continuer mon dhikr pendant mes règles ?
items.a: Oui. Le dhikr et les invocations restent disponibles pendant les jours de règles. Quand le Mode règles est activé, l’écran Dhikr renvoie aussi au guide du Mode règles, qui présente les avis des quatre madhhabs sur la lecture du Coran pendant les menstrues.

items.q: Lunora est-elle disponible sur iPhone et Android ?
items.a: Lunora est gratuite à télécharger sur l’App Store et Google Play, et sans publicité. Lunora+ est un abonnement qui ouvre l’application complète, et tu peux le commencer par un essai gratuit.

daily-duas-dhikr-muslim-women-guide.h1: The Complete Guide to Daily Duas and Dhikr for Muslim Women
daily-duas-dhikr-muslim-women-guide.body:
You wake up to your alarm, reach for your phone, and scroll through notifications before your feet even touch the floor. By the time you remember you meant to say your morning adhkar, you're already rushing out the door.

Sound familiar? You're not alone.

So many of us want a consistent dhikr practice. We know the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) described the difference between someone who remembers Allah and someone who doesn't as "the difference between the living and the dead" (Sahih Bukhari). We feel it in our hearts, that pull toward something deeper. But between work, family, studies, and the thousand small demands of daily life, our daily duas and dhikr as Muslim women end up at the bottom of the list.

This guide is your fresh start. Whether you're a complete beginner who doesn't know where to begin, or you've been making dhikr for years but want to deepen your practice, this complete guide to daily duas and dhikr for Muslim women covers everything: morning and evening adhkar, dhikr after salah, duas for every occasion, dua during menstruation, and a realistic plan to make it all stick.

No guilt. No overwhelm. Just a clear, practical path to filling your days with the remembrance of Allah.

Why daily dhikr matters for your spiritual wellbeing

Before we get into the specific duas, let's talk about why this practice is so transformative.

What the Quran says about remembrance

Allah tells us directly: "Verily, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest" (Quran 13:28).

That's not a suggestion. It's a promise. When your heart feels restless, anxious, or disconnected, dhikr is the medicine Allah Himself prescribed.

And there's a verse that speaks to us as Muslim women specifically. In Surah Al-Ahzab, Allah says: "... men who remember Allah often and women who remember Allah often, for them Allah has prepared forgiveness and a great reward" (Quran 33:35). We're named. We're included. Our dhikr carries the same weight, the same reward, the same closeness to Allah.

The spiritual and emotional benefits

Consistent dhikr does more than check a box on your spiritual to-do list. Women who build a daily practice often describe feeling:

  • Less anxious. The repetitive nature of dhikr calms the nervous system. When your mind is racing with worries about tomorrow, grounding yourself in SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, Allahu Akbar brings you back to the present moment.
  • More grateful. Dhikr trains your brain to notice blessings. When you say Alhamdulillah 33 times after every prayer, gratitude stops being an afterthought and becomes a reflex.
  • Spiritually protected. The Prophet (peace be upon him) taught specific adhkar as shields against anxiety, the evil eye, and negative whispers (waswas). These aren't abstract concepts. They're practical tools.
  • Closer to Allah. "Remember Me, and I will remember you" (Quran 2:152). There is no relationship more worth nurturing.

Amina, a 28-year-old teacher in London, struggled with anxiety for years. She'd tried journaling, meditation apps, breathing exercises. Nothing stuck. Then her mother suggested she commit to just the morning adhkar after Fajr. "The first week was hard," Amina shared. "By the third week, I noticed I wasn't reaching for my phone first thing anymore. I was reaching for Allah. The anxiety didn't vanish, but I finally had an anchor."

That anchor is available to you too. And it starts with knowing what to say.

Looking for a gentle companion for your daily dhikr? Lunora's Duas & Dhikr collection puts morning and evening adhkar right at your fingertips, beautifully organized and easy to follow.

Morning adhkar: start your day with Allah's protection

The morning adhkar are your spiritual armor for the day. The Prophet (peace be upon him) never left them, and the benefits he described are extraordinary.

When to recite your morning adhkar

The ideal time is between Fajr prayer and sunrise. That window right after you pray Fajr, while the world is still quiet, is the most powerful time for morning remembrance.

But life happens. If you miss that window, scholars agree you can recite them up until mid-morning (Dhuha time). The point is to say them. Don't let the "perfect time" become the enemy of actually doing it.

Essential morning duas every Muslim woman should know

Here are the core morning adhkar, drawn from authentic hadith:

1. Ayat al-Kursi (Quran 2:255)

Allahu la ilaha illa huwa, Al-Hayyul-Qayyum...

"Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence..."

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said whoever recites this in the morning will be protected until evening (narrated in Hakim).

2. The Three Quls

Recite Surah Al-Ikhlas (112), Surah Al-Falaq (113), and Surah An-Nas (114) three times each. These three surahs together are a comprehensive shield against harm.

3. Sayyid al-Istighfar (The Master Supplication for Forgiveness)

Allahumma anta Rabbi, la ilaha illa anta, khalaqtani wa ana 'abduka...

"O Allah, You are my Lord. There is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant..."

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever says this during the day with firm belief and dies that day before evening, they will be among the people of Paradise" (Sahih Bukhari).

4. Morning Protection Dua

Bismillahil-ladhi la yadurru ma'asmihi shay'un fil-ardi wa la fis-sama'i, wa Huwas-Sami'ul-'Alim (three times)

"In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing."

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said whoever recites this three times in the morning will not be afflicted by any sudden harm until evening (Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi).

5. SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi (100 times)

SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi

"Glory be to Allah and praise Him."

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever says this 100 times in the morning, none will come on the Day of Resurrection with anything better, except one who said the same or more" (Sahih Muslim).

A realistic 10-minute morning adhkar routine

You don't have to recite every single morning dua from day one. Here's a manageable starting point:

  1. Ayat al-Kursi (1 minute)
  2. Three Quls, three times each (2 minutes)
  3. Sayyid al-Istighfar, once (1 minute)
  4. Morning protection dua, three times (1 minute)
  5. SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, 100 times (5 minutes)

Total: about 10 minutes. That's less time than it takes to scroll through Instagram.

Evening adhkar: end your day in peace

The evening adhkar mirror the morning ones, creating a bookend of protection around your entire day.

When to recite your evening adhkar

The recommended time is between Asr prayer and Maghrib. If you miss that window, you can recite them after Maghrib or before sleep. Many scholars note that the evening extends until you sleep.

Essential evening duas and their meanings

Most of the morning adhkar are repeated in the evening with slight wording changes. These essential evening duas mirror the morning ones. The core evening adhkar include:

1. Ayat al-Kursi, same as morning, now protecting you through the night.

2. The Three Quls, three times each, just like morning.

3. Evening Protection Dua

Amsa'na wa amsal-mulku lillah, wal-hamdu lillah...

"We have entered the evening and all sovereignty belongs to Allah, and all praise is for Allah..."

4. Seeking Refuge from the Evening's Harm

A'udhu bikalimatillahit-tammati min sharri ma khalaq (three times)

"I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created."

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said whoever says this three times in the evening, no poisonous creature will harm them that night (Sahih Muslim).

5. SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, 100 times, just as in the morning.

Creating a calming evening dhikr ritual

Nadia, a mother of three in Toronto, found her sweet spot by linking evening adhkar to her children's bedtime routine. "After I tuck them in, I sit on my prayer mat for 10 minutes before I do anything else. No phone, no dishes, just me and my adhkar. It's become the most peaceful part of my day."

Try anchoring your evening adhkar to something you already do every night. After Maghrib prayer, after putting kids to bed, or right before you sleep. Consistency matters more than timing.

Dhikr after salah: the most powerful 5 minutes of your day

The moments right after you say salam in prayer are some of the most spiritually charged minutes of your entire day. The Prophet (peace be upon him) never wasted them. If you're still building your salah practice, our complete salah guide for Muslim women can help you get started.

The complete post-prayer dhikr sequence

Here's the step-by-step sequence, exactly as the Prophet (peace be upon him) practiced it:

Step 1: Istighfar (3 times)

Astaghfirullah, Astaghfirullah, Astaghfirullah

"I seek forgiveness from Allah."

Start by asking forgiveness for any shortcomings in your prayer.

Step 2: Recite Ayat al-Kursi

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi after every obligatory prayer, nothing prevents them from entering Paradise except death" (An-Nasa'i).

Step 3: The Three Quls

Surah Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, and An-Nas, once each (after every prayer) or three times each (after Fajr and Maghrib).

The tasbih guide: SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, Allahu Akbar

This is the dhikr the Prophet (peace be upon him) specifically taught his beloved daughter Fatimah (may Allah be pleased with her). When she asked him for a servant to help with housework, he gave her something better:

SubhanAllah, 33 times
Alhamdulillah, 33 times
Allahu Akbar, 34 times

"This is better for you than a servant," he told her (Sahih Bukhari).

The Prophet (peace be upon him) also said: "Whoever glorifies Allah (SubhanAllah) 33 times after every prayer, praises Allah (Alhamdulillah) 33 times, and declares His greatness (Allahu Akbar) 34 times, and then says La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamd, wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir, his sins will be forgiven even if they are like the foam of the sea" (Sahih Muslim).

That's 100 counts total. You can use your fingers, a physical tasbih (also called misbaha or dhikr beads), or a dhikr counter in an app. Following this sunnah (prophetic practice) is one of the easiest ways to fill your day with remembrance.

The entire post-prayer sequence takes about 5-6 minutes. Five prayers a day means roughly 25-30 minutes of dhikr woven into your day without adding a single extra appointment to your schedule.

Best duas for every occasion in daily life

Beyond the structured adhkar, Islam gives us beautiful duas that turn ordinary moments into acts of worship.

Duas for waking up and going to sleep

Waking up:

Alhamdu lillahil-ladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana wa ilayhin-nushur

"All praise is for Allah who gave us life after having taken it from us, and unto Him is the resurrection."

Going to sleep:

Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya

"In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live."

Also recite Ayat al-Kursi, the Three Quls, and blow into your palms and wipe over your body (Sahih Bukhari).

Duas for eating, drinking, and leaving the house

Before eating: Bismillah ("In the name of Allah")

After eating: Alhamdu lillahil-ladhi at'amana wa saqana wa ja'alana Muslimin

Leaving the house: Bismillah, tawakkaltu 'alallah, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah

"In the name of Allah, I place my trust in Allah, and there is no power or might except with Allah."

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said whoever says this when leaving their home will be told: "You are guided, defended, and protected" (Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi).

Dua for anxiety and stress in Islam

This is one of the most important duas the Prophet (peace be upon him) taught us:

Allahumma inni a'udhu bika minal-hammi wal-hazan, wal-'ajzi wal-kasal, wal-bukhli wal-jubn, wa dala'id-dayni wa ghalabatir-rijal

"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from anxiety and grief, from weakness and laziness, from miserliness and cowardice, and from the burden of debt and being overpowered by others."

Notice how comprehensive this dua is. It covers hamm (worry about the future) and hazan (grief about the past). It addresses feeling weak, feeling stuck, and feeling overwhelmed by circumstances beyond your control. If you're going through a hard season, this dua was made for you. As Yaqeen Institute's research on Islamic spirituality explains, these prophetic supplications address both spiritual and emotional dimensions of distress.

Another short but powerful dua for moments of acute stress:

Ya Hayyu Ya Qayyum, bi rahmatika astagheeth

"O Living and Eternal Sustainer, by Your mercy I seek relief!"

The Prophet (peace be upon him) would say this when afflicted with difficulty (Tirmidhi).

Dua for protection in Islam and dua for gratitude

For protection:

Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min sharri nafsi wa min sharri kulli dabbatin anta akhidhun binasiyatiha

"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my own self and from the evil of every creature that You hold by its forelock."

For gratitude:

Allahumma ma asbaha bi min ni'matin aw bi-ahadin min khalqika faminka wahdaka la sharika laka, falakal-hamdu wa lakash-shukr

"O Allah, whatever blessing I or any of Your creation received this morning is from You alone, without partner. So for You is all praise and unto You all gratitude."

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said whoever says this in the morning has fulfilled their gratitude for that day (Abu Dawud).

All of these duas, organized by occasion, are available in Lunora's Duas & Dhikr collection, so you always have them with you, even when you can't remember the Arabic by heart.

Your spiritual practice during menstruation: what you CAN do

Let's address something most Islamic content quietly ignores.

When your period starts, it can feel like your entire spiritual routine grinds to a halt. No salah. Possibly no Quran recitation (depending on scholarly opinion). It's easy to feel disconnected, left out, even spiritually abandoned. If you've been wondering about all the rules, our complete guide to prayer during your period breaks it down in detail.

But here's what many women don't realize: dua and dhikr have absolutely no restrictions during menstruation. None. This is the consensus of Islamic scholars across all schools of thought.

Duas and dhikr you can recite during your period

Every dua during menstruation listed in this guide, every single dhikr, is fully permitted during your period:

  • Morning and evening adhkar, fully permitted
  • SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, Allahu Akbar, fully permitted
  • Istighfar, fully permitted
  • Dua for anxiety, protection, gratitude, fully permitted
  • Salawat upon the Prophet, fully permitted
  • Any dua in any language, fully permitted

The scholars at SeekersGuidance confirm that a menstruating woman can engage in dhikr, dua, istighfar, salawat, and listening to the Quran without any restriction.

Regarding Quran recitation specifically, scholarly opinions vary. The Hanafi school generally restricts reciting Quran from memory during menstruation, while the Maliki school and many contemporary scholars permit it. If you follow a school that restricts Quran recitation, you can still recite Quranic verses with the intention of dua, not recitation. For more on navigating your Quran practice, see our Quran reading guide for Muslim women. Consult your local scholar for guidance specific to your situation.

Adjusting your daily routine during menstruation

Since you're not praying salah during your period, you lose those natural "dhikr anchor points" throughout the day. Here's how to adapt:

  1. Keep your morning and evening adhkar exactly the same. These aren't tied to salah.
  2. At prayer times, sit on your mat and do your tasbih. 33-33-34. Same as always. You're just not praying salah before it.
  3. Increase your dua. Without the structure of salah, free-form dua in your own language becomes even more powerful. Talk to Allah about your day, your worries, your gratitude.
  4. Listen to Quran if your school restricts recitation. Listening carries its own reward.
  5. Journal your gratitude. Pair your dhikr practice with reflection.

Yasmin, a university student in Kuala Lumpur, used to dread her period because she felt spiritually "shut down." Then she discovered that the restrictions were far narrower than she'd assumed. "When I learned I could still do ALL my adhkar, it changed everything. My period became a time of deeper dua, not less worship. I actually look forward to those quieter conversations with Allah now."

Why your spiritual journey doesn't pause

Your body is going through a natural process that Allah created. You are not impure. You are not less. And your spiritual life is not on hold.

Lunora's Period Mode was built for exactly this. It offers gentle spiritual guidance during menstruation, showing you exactly what you CAN do, with adapted duas and dhikr for your cycle days. Because your faith journey includes all of you.

How to build a daily dua habit that actually sticks

Knowing which duas to say is only half the equation. The other half is actually saying them consistently. As a Muslim woman with a full life, you need a framework that fits your reality, not an idealized version of it. Here's what works.

Start with just 3 duas (the beginner's approach)

If you're starting from zero, don't try to memorize all the adhkar at once. Pick three:

  1. Ayat al-Kursi after every prayer (or twice daily if not praying during your period)
  2. The morning protection dua (Bismillahil-ladhi la yadurru...) three times after Fajr
  3. SubhanAllah wa bihamdihi 100 times (split it: 50 in the morning, 50 in the evening)

Do these for two weeks. Once they feel natural, add the next layer.

Anchor your dhikr to existing daily routines

Habit research shows that the most effective way to build a new habit is to attach it to something you already do. This is called "habit stacking."

  • After Fajr prayer → morning adhkar (you're already on the mat)
  • During your commute → listen to adhkar audio or count SubhanAllah on your fingers
  • While cooking dinner → recite istighfar or salawat quietly
  • After putting kids to bed → evening adhkar (the house is finally quiet)
  • Before you sleep → Ayat al-Kursi + Three Quls + sleep dua

The key is linking dhikr to a trigger you never skip.

Track your progress and celebrate consistency

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The most beloved deeds to Allah are those done consistently, even if they are small" (Sahih Bukhari).

Consistency beats intensity. Saying your morning adhkar every single day for a month is more valuable than doing a marathon dhikr session once and then nothing for weeks.

Keep a simple tracker. A checklist on your fridge, a note in your phone, or a habit-tracking app. Check off each day you complete your adhkar. Watch the streak grow. Let momentum carry you.

Using Lunora to make daily dhikr easier

One of the biggest barriers to consistent dhikr is simply not having the duas accessible when you need them. You know you should say the morning adhkar, but you can't remember the full Arabic, and your Hisn al-Muslim book is on a shelf somewhere.

Lunora solves this by putting a curated, beautifully organized dua collection right on your phone. Morning adhkar, evening adhkar, duas for every occasion, all with Arabic text, transliteration, and English translation. And during your period, Period Mode adjusts your content so you see exactly what's relevant to your cycle days.

It's not another prayer alarm. It's a gentle spiritual companion that meets you where you are.

The spiritual benefits of dhikr: what happens when you're consistent

When you commit to daily duas and dhikr as a Muslim woman, something shifts. It doesn't happen overnight, but it happens. The barakah (blessing) of consistency builds slowly, the way dawn light fills a room.

Inner peace and reduced anxiety

Remember Quran 13:28: "In the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest."

This isn't just a spiritual concept. The rhythmic, repetitive nature of dhikr, saying SubhanAllah over and over, counting through your tasbih, creates a meditative state that many women find deeply calming. It's not a replacement for professional mental health support when you need it. But as a daily spiritual practice, consistent dhikr gives your anxious mind a place to rest.

Stronger connection with Allah

"So remember Me; I will remember you" (Quran 2:152).

The more you talk to Allah throughout your day, the more you feel His presence. This is tawakkul (trust in Allah) in its most practical form. Dhikr transforms your relationship with your Creator from scheduled appointments (the five prayers) to an ongoing, constant conversation. You begin to see His hand in everything, to whisper Alhamdulillah at sunsets and SubhanAllah at small miracles.

Protection from negative thoughts and waswas

The Shaytaan's whispers thrive in silence. When your tongue and heart are busy with dhikr, there's less room for doubt, despair, and self-criticism. The morning and evening adhkar specifically include duas for protection from evil, from envy, and from harm. They're not just words. They're a fortress, which is exactly why the famous dua collection is called Hisn al-Muslim (Fortress of the Muslim).

Building gratitude as a daily practice

When you say Alhamdulillah 33 times after each prayer, you're training your heart to look for things to be grateful for. Over time, gratitude stops being something you practice and becomes something you are. You start noticing the small blessings: the warm cup of tea, the child's laugh, the fact that you woke up at all.

Pair your dhikr with Lunora's Gratitude Journal to deepen this practice. Write down three things you're grateful for each day alongside your evening adhkar. Watch how your perspective shifts over weeks and months.

Frequently asked questions about daily duas and dhikr

Can I make dhikr during my period?

Yes, absolutely. There are no restrictions on dua, dhikr, istighfar, or salawat during menstruation. This is the consensus of Islamic scholars across all schools of thought. The only worship that pauses during your period is salah and (in some scholarly opinions) Quran recitation from the mushaf.

What is the best dhikr to say daily?

The most rewarding daily dhikr is the post-prayer tasbih: SubhanAllah 33 times, Alhamdulillah 33 times, Allahu Akbar 34 times. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said this practice can erase sins "even if they are like the foam of the sea." Combined with Ayat al-Kursi after each prayer, this forms the foundation of a powerful daily practice.

How long should morning adhkar take?

A basic morning adhkar routine takes about 10 minutes: Ayat al-Kursi (1 min), the Three Quls three times each (2 min), Sayyid al-Istighfar (1 min), the morning protection dua three times (1 min), and SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi 100 times (5 min). You can start with just 2-3 duas and build up gradually.

What dua helps with anxiety in Islam?

The most comprehensive dua for anxiety is: "Allahumma inni a'udhu bika minal-hammi wal-hazan..." ("O Allah, I seek refuge in You from anxiety and grief, from weakness and laziness..."). For acute moments of stress, the Prophet (peace be upon him) would say: "Ya Hayyu Ya Qayyum, bi rahmatika astagheeth" ("O Living and Eternal Sustainer, by Your mercy I seek relief").

Your daily dhikr, starting today

You don't need to overhaul your entire life to become someone who remembers Allah throughout the day. You just need to start.

Here's your simple action plan:

  1. Pick your first three duas from this guide (Ayat al-Kursi, morning protection dua, and tasbih are a great starting trio)
  2. Anchor them to Fajr or another consistent daily trigger
  3. Keep them accessible on your phone or a printed card by your prayer mat
  4. Track your consistency for 30 days
  5. Add more gradually as the first three become second nature

And on the days you forget? No guilt. No shame. Just start again tomorrow. Allah loves the servant who keeps returning to Him.

"Those who remember Allah while standing, sitting, and lying on their sides" (Quran 3:191). Standing in the kitchen. Sitting at your desk. Lying in bed after a long day. Your daily duas and dhikr fit into every posture of your life, every season of your body, every chapter of your journey as a Muslim woman.
